title: India Explorer
description: A tile cartogram (not a traced map) with one equal tile for each of India's 28 states and 8 union territories. Tiles can be colored by the language family of each place's main official language or by informal region. Tapping a tile shows its capital, official languages, language family and a short note. A caption marks it as schematic, and a note states that the wider Kashmir region is disputed.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: South Asian cultures
Geography
India
Civics
Languages
publisher: Roots & Rivers: An Interactive Guide to South Asian Cultures for High School Students
audience: Students, Educators, South Asian student club leaders
learningObjectives: Name India's states and union territories and find their capitals.
Explain how many state borders were drawn around languages (linguistic states).
Classify states by the language family of their official languages and by region.
prerequisites: Knowing the eight countries of South Asia (Chapter 1)
Knowing the main language families of South Asia (Chapter 6)
keyQuestions: What is the difference between a state and a union territory?
Why do so many states have their own official language?
Where in India are Dravidian and Tibeto-Burman languages the main official languages?
misconceptions: Hindi is spoken everywhere in India.
A bigger tile means a bigger state.
